title: Part 2.II — Agent in General
role: Second Part-2 chapter. Agent is the term idealism features as the locus of motive: the constituting subject (mind, ego, consciousness, will) is the originating ground from which action proceeds. Burke walks the modern idealist lineage from Berkeley through Hume (treated as a transitional figure rather than a Humean skeptic against idealism), Leibniz, Kant (with three consecutive subsections including 'Moral Transcendence in Kant' covering the Critiques and the practical-reason move), Idealism After Kant, Hegel, and then — crucially — extends into Marxism / Communist Manifesto / Lenin, arguing that historical materialism is itself Agent-featuring because class-as-collective-agent is its motive-locus despite the materialist surface-vocabulary. Closes with Santayana (Tier-A interlocutor per Phase 0 cite-check, 42 hits volume-wide) and a subsection on imagination. The single most demographically populous chapter for Tier-A philosophers in the volume.

Phase 0 cite-check flags Santayana for Tier-A elevation; the dedicated 9-page subsection here confirms.
